summary: Removed the "intro" and "details" pre-email funnel steps and changed the CTA from "자세히 알아보기" (Learn more) to "무료로 시작하기" (Start for free) linking directly to email capture, because every extra step before email entry loses 20–40% of users and a passive "learn more" CTA delays commitment with no payoff.

Replaced the bare, friction-heavy landing page with a styled hero section featuring a benefit-driven headline, three trust-reducing objection busters ("no credit card," "30-second signup," "cancel anytime"), a prominent red CTA button, and social proof — all of which lower perceived risk and increase the likelihood a visitor clicks through to the email step.

Replaced the external CTA link with an inline email input form so users can enter their email without an extra page load, eliminating one click of friction — the single biggest lever for signup conversion rates.

Moved the social proof (star rating + 12,000-user count) to appear directly above the email form, because showing trust signals at the moment of decision — rather than after the CTA — reduces last-second hesitation and increases form submissions.

Added a specific testimonial with a named user and a concrete outcome ("2주 만에 업무 처리 속도 향상") because named social proof converts better than anonymous statistics — it answers the visitor's implicit "will this work for someone like me?" objection and makes the benefit feel real and achievable.

Removed the "verify" step from the funnel, cutting it from 4 steps to 3, because email verification is a well-documented high-dropout friction point that can eliminate 20–40% of signups before they complete.
